source_acquisition.search_note: The PDF explicitly links the author repository harrya32/hyperparameter-trajectory-inference in Appendix C and the reproducibility statement. gh metadata/tree inspection confirms the author repository and its HTI predecessor, plus the listed evaluator scripts, notebooks, and dropout diagnostic plots; no committed Figure 1–5 composite, target report TeX, or exact figure-generation script was found. The local inventory selected dnkit24/sinkhorn-hti because its README title is exact and it contains report/table_results.tex and sinkhorn-hti/scripts/regenerate_figs.py, but those files belong to an entropic-OT course-project report: the script produces a 2×4 L-BFGS/entropic trajectory figure and the table reports a different wall-time/NLL/CD comparison. They are therefore not counted as exact target sources. The status is partial_visual_source because related author plotting/data pathways are available while exact target visual sources are absent.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Main plots use a Matplotlib-like categorical palette: blue/orange/green/red/purple/brown identify methods or conditions, and pale same-color fills represent trajectory/interval variation. Figure 2 uses blue versus red for true/surrogate; Figure 3 uses a green true interval plus method colors; Figure 4 uses blue/red conceptual manifolds. Tables remain monochrome booktabs with directional arrows and parenthetical standard errors.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: The 200 dpi page renders show vector/text content for Figures 1–3 and 5, captions, rules, and tables. Figure 4 is the sole embedded raster object: eight 512×512 RGB images with alpha masks at 2812 ppi on p.16, surrounded by vector caption/text. Thus the paper is vector-dominant with one raster conceptual diagram.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman No9 L and Computer Modern math dominate body, captions, equations, and tables; DejaVu Sans Type3 appears in plot/raster labels. Booktabs rules, centered headers, and compact method/metric tables are stable across main and appendix. Figure 3/4 label density and color dependence are the main local departures from the otherwise restrained style.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Dots represent true samples from the temporal process across t ∈ [0, 1], lines represent model estimated trajectories from t = 0 to t = 1. Each condition has a distinct colour.

color.semantic_mapping: Four condition identities use blue, red, green, and purple; lighter colored true dots indicate larger t, while same-color paths indicate the estimated trajectory for that condition.

encodings.color: condition c; lightness of true dots indicates larger t
encodings.shape: small dots for true samples; line paths for estimates
encodings.facet: four Lagrangian variants K_I, K_I−Û, K_θ, K_θ−Û

figures.data_and_statistics: Synthetic conditional semicircle process with four conditions, three observed times t∈{0,0.5,1}, and 100 samples per condition/time. Each panel shows colored true samples and multiple inferred paths; held-out t∈{0.25,0.75} are evaluated in Table 1. No aggregate uncertainty or numeric axis scale is encoded.
figures.evidence_relation: §4 learned metric and density potential → four matched ablations in Figure 1 → withheld-time NLL/CD in Table 1 → claim that both inductive biases recover non-Euclidean conditional paths.
design_strengths: Matched coordinate frames make curvature and condition crossing comparable.
Four panels expose the separate and joint effects of metric and potential.
Dots/lines and time lightness create a compact true-versus-estimated visual key.
design_weaknesses: Condition identity is primarily color-coded and is not grayscale-safe.
Dense dots and paths overlap, while axes carry no numeric ticks or units.
The caption does not name the four panels or define the lightness/time mapping.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a common coordinate frame and matched ablation panels to show how each mechanism changes a geometric path.

evidence.label: Figure 1; p.7 rendered figure and caption

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4: Example inference-time adjustment enabled by HTI. We illustrate disparate user preferences affecting desired NN behaviour (desired λ level) for different users in this abstract example. Having a fixed number of trained NNs (p_{θ_{λ_i}}) only allows partial exploration of the full hyperparameter trajectory, while an HTI surrogate model ((p̂(·|x_i, λ))_{λ∈Λ}) can estimate outputs across the entire spectrum of hyperparameters (estimated conditional probability paths represented by solid blue/red lines). Crucially, hyperparameter-induced dynamics can differ amongst input conditions (x_i), as the true conditional distributions move along their own respective manifolds (M_{x_i}), so an effective HTI model must learn conditional dynamics.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue/red manifolds and paths represent two conditional input cases; pale fills show manifolds, black/gray labels and connectors show anchors, users, and λ requests, and peach icons show user instances.

encodings.x: left conceptual ambient space; right user-demand lane
encodings.y: conditional manifolds and vertical λ request list
encodings.color: input-condition/manifold identity and solid path identity
encodings.shape: point clouds, manifold envelopes, user icons, brace
encodings.line: solid conditional paths and dotted anchor-to-demand connectors
encodings.facet: left distribution geometry versus right finite-anchor/user requests
encodings.text: p_{θ_{λ_i}}, M_{x_i}, λ levels, brace, and R^d label

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual example rather than a measured dataset; sparse anchor distributions are shown for two input conditions and user-specific desired λ levels. The panel contains no statistical uncertainty, sample denominator, or quantitative axis.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix A’s inference-time adjustment interface → Figure 4’s sparse anchors/continuous conditional paths → main Figure 1 and Algorithm 2’s path construction and sampling → claim that HTI supports conditional, user-specific adjustment.
design_strengths: The geometry lane and user-demand lane make the method interface concrete.
Solid/dotted paths, labels, and spatial grouping redundantly distinguish anchors from inferred trajectories.
The caption explicitly states the conditional-dynamics mechanism and fixed-anchor comparison.
design_weaknesses: The embedded raster tiles and small formulas are less robust to zoom and grayscale.
The long caption carries much of the interpretation and arrives after the main results.
User λ examples are abstract and do not show a measured output or task metric.
figures.reusable_pattern: Show sparse anchors and continuous conditional paths in one conceptual plane, with a separate demand lane connecting geometry to inference-time use.

evidence.label: Figure 4; p.16 rendered figure and caption

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 and Table 1 establish the learned metric/density-potential mechanism on conditional semicircles; Tables 2–4 transfer the same surrogate suite to linear and nonlinear reward weighting; Table 5 and Figure 3 transfer it to quantile intervals; Table 6 and Table 7 close the main-text generative and metric-parameterization tests; Figure 5 then probes the sparsity boundary in Appendix E. Algorithms 1–2 and Tables 8–15 provide training, sampling, and reproduction support.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions generally combine a title with a metric/evaluation grid and comparison. Figure 1 and Figure 3 decode visual marks or row order, while result-table captions name held-out settings but defer 20-run standard-error semantics to §5. Figure 4 is the most self-contained caption; Figure 5 is title-only and leaves the band and sparsity interpretation to prose.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables 1–6 use compact Method plus a directional metric header (NLL/CD/Reward/MSE/WD); Table 7 adds grouped task headers and repeats arrows; Tables 8–15 use Hyperparameter/Value. Booktabs top/mid/bottom rules and no cell colors keep the table family coherent.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1/Table 1 isolate the density potential and learned metric, while Table 7 isolates eigenvalue parameterization across four 2-D tasks. Tables 2–6 evaluate the full method and baselines on policy, forecast, and distribution metrics, preserving the mechanism-to-result chain.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main objects point readers to Appendix C for datasets, model settings, and training protocols. Appendix A Figure 4 explains the inference-time interface, Appendix B Algorithm 2 explains sampling, Tables 8–15 expose hyperparameters, and Appendix E Figure 5 tests the sparsity limit of the headline interpolation claim.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: PDF text uses a stable Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern family, with DejaVu Sans-like plot labels. Table body/header scale is consistent across main and appendix; small multiples and the raster conceptual panel compress local legibility.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: The same categorical method colors recur across interval and sparsity plots, while Figure 1 and Figure 4 use blue/red or four-condition palettes for geometry. Color is semantically coherent but rarely paired with distinct marker or line-style identities, so grayscale robustness is weak.

most_reusable_patterns: Matched mechanism-ablation panels plus a withheld-time table.
One-metric result tables with explicit directional arrows and held-out grids.
Method×instance interval small multiples with shared scales and one legend.
Matched task panels using anchor density as a robustness axis.
Stable booktabs Method/metric and Hyperparameter/Value table grammars.
failure_patterns: Captions defer standard-error/band definitions and sample denominators to body text.
Figure 5 has no finding or uncertainty statement in its caption.
Color carries most method/condition identity and degrades in grayscale.
Figure 3 and Figure 4 are label-dense at page scale.
Exact target figure/table source files are absent from the public author repository.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Use compact geometry and interval visuals to make conditional trajectories inspectable, then repeat a disciplined one-metric table grammar across application settings and place reproducibility and sparsity boundaries in the appendix.
